summary: Executed the task 7.3 verification of the GOALS.md success criteria end-to-end on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host (http://127.0.0.1:8096, prefix /tmp/jf) with no live Sonarr/Radarr, per the approved scope. Added committed test-support fixtures: scripts/mock-arr-fixture.cs, a .NET 10 file-based app (not in ArrTags.slnx, no plugin dependency) that serves the exact /api/v3 read endpoints the clients call, enforces X-Api-Key, logs one line per request (method/path/query/key-validity/status/file, never the key value), reads payloads from disk so a changed observation is reproducible without restart, and can simulate a provider outage; plus scripts/mock-arr-fixtures/ with representative payloads (tmdbId/tvdbId/imdbId, quality, mediaInfo, custom formats, and a sparse optional-fields-absent record per ADR-013). Created a real Jellyfin Movie and Series/Episode with local .nfo provider ids and real poster images, added the libraries, and completed the startup wizard for authenticated access; the plugin was configured by writing data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml and restarting (runtime configuration replacement is a documented Phase 7 deferral). RESULTS: GOALS criteria 1 (loads on Jellyfin 12), 2 (independent provider enablement - Sonarr-only called only Sonarr, Radarr-only called only Radarr, both called both, each with a valid X-Api-Key and no call to the disabled provider), 3 (movie matched Radarr movie 1/file 11 by TMDb 990001 and the episode matched Sonarr series 1/episode 101/file 201 by TVDB 990004; persisted state records Matched/ProviderId), 4 (actual file quality retrieved: Bluray-1080p/bluray/1080 and WEBDL-1080p/webdl/1080 plus media-info resolution, dynamic range, codecs, channels, custom formats, upgrade-pending), and 9 (reproducible build/package; suite counts unchanged) are MET. Criterion 7 is met only at the contract level (EnhancedCoexistenceTests 7/7; Jellyfin Enhanced is not installed live). RELEASE BLOCKER 7.3-F1: criteria 5, 6, and 8 are NOT met as shipped. With the committed package, publishing the first badge through Jellyfin's supported IProviderManager.SaveImage path aborts the host with a fatal System.InvalidCastException between the host default-context SkiaSharp.UserDataDelegate (/tmp/jf/jellyfin/SkiaSharp.dll) and the plugin-context one (/tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll). Reproduced on two independent runs; it occurs ~8 ms after the artwork-operation record is written; it does not occur with both providers disabled or with the plugin uninstalled; and removing the bundled SkiaSharp.dll + libSkiaSharp.so from the installed plugin folder (so the plugin shares the host's SkiaSharp) makes the whole pipeline work, so the conflict is the bundled duplicate, not the render/publication logic. Under that diagnostic install the rest of criterion 5/6/8 behavior is correct: the movie and episode badges were served anonymously by GET /Items/{id}/Images/Primary (image/png, 30,752 and 32,400 bytes; served SHA-256 equal to the persisted PublishedArtworkState.ActiveImageIdentity), the original poster.jpg and S01E01.jpg were byte-unchanged, the retained SourceArtifactId equalled the original poster SHA-256, a changed mock quality (1080p -> 2160p/HDR10) produced new metadata and publication fingerprints, a new image tag, and new served bytes, an unchanged re-run left the tag/fingerprint/bytes identical, and stopping the mock left the host up with the current artwork unchanged and the last-known-good metadata marked stale. No production code or package content was changed; the SkiaSharp removal was applied only to the temporary installed folder. A packaging/architecture decision (new ADR) plus build.yaml and PluginPackagingTests changes are required before V1 release; ready_for_next_task is false. Host returned to a clean running state (no ArrTags install/state/config, zero libraries, no [ERR]/[FTL]); /tmp/7.3 removed.
validation: `. /config/arrtags-env.sh && ./build.sh build` -> Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) (net10.0, pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0).

`. /config/arrtags-env.sh && ./build.sh package` -> artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip (5,475,666 bytes); installed by extracting into /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0 and restarting via scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh /tmp/jf. Console: 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0' (1 load), 0 [ERR]/[FTL].
Default suite: `. /config/arrtags-env.sh && ./build.sh test` -> Failed 0, Passed 1219, Skipped 60, Total 1279, identical to the task 7.7 baseline (this verification task adds no product tests).
Host-guarded suite: `ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR=/tmp/jf/jellyfin . /config/arrtags-env.sh; ./build.sh test` -> Failed 0, Passed 1235, Skipped 44, Total 1279, identical to the task 7.7 baseline.

Enhanced contract tests: `dotnet test ArrTags.slnx -c Release --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~EnhancedCoexistenceTests"` -> Passed 7, Failed 0, Skipped 0, Total 7 (contract-level only; Jellyfin Enhanced is not installed on the host).

Mock Arr fixture readiness: with ARRTAGS_MOCK_RADARR_KEY=radarrkey123 and ARRTAGS_MOCK_SONARR_KEY=sonarrkey456, `curl -H 'X-Api-Key: radarrkey123' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/system/status` -> 200, `curl http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/movie` (no key) -> 401, `curl -H 'X-Api-Key: nope' http://127.0.0.1:8989/api/v3/series` -> 401, `curl -H 'X-Api-Key: sonarrkey456' http://127.0.0.1:8989/api/v3/series` -> 200; the request log recorded apiKey=valid/missing/invalid per request without the key value.

Independent provider configuration (live): Sonarr-only config run made only sonarr GET /api/v3/series, /api/v3/episode?seriesId=1&includeEpisodeFile=true, /api/v3/episodeFile?seriesId=1; Radarr-only config run made only radarr GET /api/v3/movie and /api/v3/moviefile?movieId=1; both-enabled run made both sets. Disabled providers were never queried.

Matching (live), from /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags/cache/metadata-state/*.json decoded PayloadJson: movie 792e65fe1e6849a5ef7584d27495da74 MatchStatus=Matched MatchMethod=ProviderId RecordIdentity MovieId=1 MovieFileId=11 MatchedProviderIds Tmdb=990001; episode e26fb220588685f9a010ca8dcb003d21 MatchStatus=Matched MatchMethod=ProviderId RecordIdentity SeriesId=1 EpisodeId=101 EpisodeFileId=201 MatchedProviderIds Tvdb=990004.

Quality retrieval (live), from the same state: movie QualityLabel='Bluray-1080p' QualitySource='bluray' QualityResolution=1080 QualityProviderId=7 ResolutionWidth=1920 ResolutionHeight=1080 DynamicRangeProfile='SDR' VideoCodec='h264' AudioCodec='DTS-HD MA' AudioChannels=5.1 CustomBadges=['x264']; episode QualityLabel='WEBDL-1080p' QualitySource='webdl' QualityResolution=1080 ResolutionWidth=1920 ResolutionHeight=1080 DynamicRangeProfile='SDR' VideoCodec='h264' AudioCodec='AAC' AudioChannels=2 UpgradePending=true CustomBadges=['WEB-DL']; both metadata states carried distinct MetadataFingerprint values.

Release blocker 7.3-F1 reproduced (run 1, Sonarr-only config): console logged 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0', the Sonarr read/map occurred, and the process ended with '[FTL] Main: Unhandled Exception System.InvalidCastException: [A]SkiaSharp.UserDataDelegate cannot be cast to [B]SkiaSharp.UserDataDelegate' at /tmp/jf/jellyfin/SkiaSharp.dll (Default) vs /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll (PluginLoadContext #1), with a non-terminal artwork-operation left for e26fb220588685f9a010ca8dcb003d21-Primary.

Release blocker 7.3-F1 reproduced (run 2, both providers enabled): the artwork-operation for movie 792e65fe1e6849a5ef7584d27495da74-Primary was written at 23:15:50.246 and the fatal InvalidCastException line at 23:15:50.254; the same A/B types were reported. Host did not recover (connection refused after the crash).

Control (both providers disabled, plugin installed): library scan + post-scan ArrTagsPostScanTask ran with 0 [FTL]/InvalidCast lines and the host stayed up (HTTP 200), so the crash requires ArrTags artwork publication, not mere plugin presence or Jellyfin's own image processing.

Control (plugin uninstalled): a library refresh with both posters processed produced 0 [FTL]/InvalidCast lines and the host stayed up (only pre-existing non-fatal SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz collection-collage typeface [ERR] lines, also present with no plugin).

Diagnostic fix direction: removing SkiaSharp.dll and libSkiaSharp.so from the installed plugin folder (keeping ArrTags.dll etc.) made the plugin share the host's SkiaSharp; a library refresh then completed with 0 [FTL], both providers were queried with valid keys, and authoritative artwork-state records were written for both items.

Criterion 5 evidence (diagnostic install): `curl http://127.0.0.1:8096/Items/792e65fe-1e68-49a5-ef75-84d27495da74/Images/Primary` -> HTTP 200 Content-Type image/png Content-Length 30752 sha256 00bdd13a0022a640dfe294ff513bd13a04bfdccbce33b39ad9135feee8f0edb8, equal to the persisted ActiveImageIdentity; `curl .../Items/e26fb220588685f9a010ca8dcb003d21/Images/Primary` -> HTTP 200 image/png 32400 bytes sha256 59490a9be6d6308d3f450500f669054823a9f04a8d09a233635873fdd84881af, equal to that item's ActiveImageIdentity; both routes are anonymous.

Source preservation evidence (diagnostic install): `sha256sum /tmp/7.3/media/movies/ArrTagsTestMovie2020/poster.jpg` -> e23a4e0998fd4750930182b48951b395564e7f6eff48ed559fa4b04dd347874f and `/tmp/7.3/media/tv/ArrTagsTestShow/Season 01/ArrTagsTestShow.S01E01.jpg` -> the same value, byte-unchanged after publication; the persisted SourceArtifactId/SourceCaptureIdentity equalled E23A4E0998FD4750930182B48951B395564E7F6EFF48ED559FA4B04DD347874F (the original poster SHA-256) and differed from the published ActiveImageIdentity hash.

Criterion 6 evidence (diagnostic install): an unchanged metadata re-run left the item ImageTags.Primary, the PublishedFingerprint, the MetadataFingerprint, and the served Primary bytes identical for both items (movie tag f87c31cccccf12e1846813b7ab6a86a8/bytes 00bdd13a; episode tag a34b3caa3abb2c5aa973f2c143c8602a/bytes 59490a9b). After changing the mock quality from 1080p to 2160p/HDR10, a re-run changed the metadata fingerprint (movie 7381318C->C656FB2E, episode E1D2CD74->D1E413CF), the PublishedFingerprint (7B0E8974->CCA00F41, 44D5556C->08CBDB35), the item image tag (movie f87c31cc->11197427, episode a34b3caa->cf491e7a), and the served bytes (movie 00bdd13a->4e356ece, episode 59490a9b->87ef0638). A subsequent unchanged re-run left them all unchanged again.

Criterion 8 evidence (diagnostic install): after killing the mock, a scheduled reconciliation left the host up (HTTP 200 across 10 polls), the served movie/episode bytes and image tags unchanged, and both metadata states converted to State=1 (stale) with no LastError and no [FTL].

Approved-trigger evidence: reconciliation was driven by the real Jellyfin 12 extension points - the post-scan task (console 'Running post-scan task 1/9: ArrTagsPostScanTask' / 'completed') and the scheduled task (GET /ScheduledTasks reported 'ArrTags: reconcile badge metadata' id 0e96fc3004bcd22db45dd641e63e2666; POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/<id> returned 204), not by calling plugin internals.

Runtime configuration mechanism: because runtime configuration replacement is a documented Phase 7 deferral, the plugin was configured by writing /tmp/jf/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml and restarting the host; each config change was confirmed loaded (the provider enable flags and base URLs took effect as observed in the mock request log).

Host returned to a clean state: test libraries removed via DELETE /Library/VirtualFolders (HTTP 204 both; 0 remaining), the mock stopped, /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0, /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags and /tmp/jf/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml removed, and the host restarted: 0 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags' lines, 0 [ERR]/[FTL], /System/Info/Public Version 12.0.0; /tmp/7.3 removed.

`git status --short` after completion: only PLANS.md, README.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/changelog.md, docs/implementation-readiness.md, docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md, the new scripts/mock-arr-fixture.cs and scripts/mock-arr-fixtures/, and this report; build.yaml, Directory.Build.props, src/ and tests/ are unchanged (no version bump); artifacts/ is gitignored and holds the intended ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip.
known_limitations: RELEASE BLOCKER 7.3-F1 (GOALS.md criteria 5, 6, and 8 not met as shipped; Phase 7 acceptance criteria 3 and 4 remain unchecked). The committed package ships SkiaSharp.dll and libSkiaSharp.so at the plugin folder root. On the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host, publishing the first badge through the supported IProviderManager.SaveImage path aborts the whole Jellyfin process with System.InvalidCastException between the host default-context SkiaSharp.UserDataDelegate (/tmp/jf/jellyfin/SkiaSharp.dll) and the plugin-context one (/tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll). It is deterministic (two runs), occurs ~8 ms after the artwork-operation write, does not occur with both providers disabled or with the plugin uninstalled, and disappears when the two bundled SkiaSharp files are removed from the installed folder so the plugin shares the host's SkiaSharp. This is a fatal Jellyfin-affecting failure, needs a new packaging/architecture decision (ADR) plus build.yaml and PluginPackagingTests changes, and was deliberately not implemented by this verification task.

Criteria 5 (badge rendered and published via the standard route with the source preserved), 6 (update/no-repeated-processing), and 8 (graceful failure) were verified only under the diagnostic install that removed the duplicate SkiaSharp from the installed plugin folder; they are NOT verified for the committed release artifact, because that artifact crashes the host on first publication. The pipeline logic itself is therefore validated, but the shipped package fails these criteria.

GOALS criterion 7 (Jellyfin Enhanced compatibility) was verified only at the contract level by EnhancedCoexistenceTests (7/7 passing). Jellyfin Enhanced is not installed on the pinned host and was not exercised live, so no live coexistence evidence exists. This is an approved scope gap, not an environment regression.

No live Sonarr or Radarr was available; provider behavior was exercised against the committed mock fixture rather than a real Sonarr 3.x-4.x / Radarr 3.x-6.x instance, so real-release payload-shape variance beyond the fixtures is untested (covered separately by the ADR-013 provider-contract fixtures).

The crash mechanism (duplicate managed SkiaSharp plus duplicate native libSkiaSharp.so with the same SONAME) was diagnosed on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host only, whose bundled native /tmp/jf/jellyfin/libSkiaSharp.so (18,453,464 bytes) differs from the plugin's NuGet copy (11,170,296 bytes). The same fatal type-identity conflict is expected on other hosts because two managed SkiaSharp copies still share type identity mismatch, but that was not verified on a glibc host.

The plugin was configured by editing the configuration XML and restarting only because runtime configuration replacement wiring is a documented Phase 7 deferral; live runtime replacement of the configuration was not exercised.

The diagnostic install that removed SkiaSharp.dll + libSkiaSharp.so left ArrTags.deps.json in the plugin folder; the plugin still rendered and published successfully by resolving the host's SkiaSharp, so the finding (share the host's SkiaSharp) is demonstrated, but the exact minimal or preferred fix (managed only, native only, or host-shared) needs the follow-up ADR to decide.

The host's own collection-folder collage image provider logs non-fatal ERR lines ('ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter typeface)' in SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz.SKShaper) on this musl host with and without ArrTags, because no usable system font is available for the collage; this is a pre-existing host condition, not caused by the plugin.

Completing the startup wizard and creating an admin user/libraries changed the pinned host's persisted database (the host was previously at StartupWizardCompleted=false with no library). The plugin install, plugin state, plugin config, and test libraries were removed and the host is running clean, but the wizard-complete flag and the admin user remain; this was necessary to authenticate and is documented rather than reverted.
